title: You keep saying you’re waiting for your moment.
paragraphs: You keep saying you’re waiting for your moment.
But heaven is looking at you like… you are the answer.
“Then He said to His disciples, ‘The harvest truly is plentiful, but the laborers are few.’” — Matthew 9:37
The problem was never the harvest.
It was the absence of people willing to step into it.
And that hit me harder than I expected.
Because I used to think the world was too far gone… too cold… too resistant. I blamed culture. I blamed sin. I blamed “the times.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Jesus never said the harvest was the issue.
Souls searching in the dark. People silently breaking behind smiles. Addictions hidden. Questions unanswered. Hearts wide open… but no one showing up with truth.
The real question wasn’t, “Why aren’t people coming to God?”
“Why aren’t God’s people going to them?”
I remember the moment it became personal.
But in a quiet, ordinary interaction… where I felt that nudge to speak, to share, to say His name—and I didn’t.
And that’s when the weight of Matthew 9:37 stopped being a verse… and started becoming a mirror.
Jesus looked at crowds and felt compassion, Scripture says, because they were “harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd” (Matthew 9:36).
That means the harvest isn’t just numbers.
It’s people trying everything except the One who can actually save them.
And we’re surrounded by them every day.
But the tragedy isn’t just that they’re lost.
It’s that many who are found… stay silent.
There’s a dangerous comfort in knowing truth but never speaking it.
In being saved… but never sent.
In receiving grace… but never extending it.
And slowly, without realizing it, faith becomes private… contained… convenient.
And laborers get their hands dirty.
They carry truth into places where it’s not always welcomed.
“He who believes in the Son has everlasting life; and he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.” — John 3:36
The lesson I learned from “the harvest is plenty but workers are few” wasn’t motivational.
It stripped away comfort and replaced it with responsibility.
Not to save people—that’s God’s work.
“To whom much is given, from him much will be required.” — Luke 12:48
So what are you doing with it?
Because there are only two directions this goes.
Either you continue observing from a distance… convincing yourself someone else will step in…
Or you become the one who says, “Send me.”
And yes, it will stretch you.
Yes, it will confront your fear.
Yes, it will expose your hesitation.
But it will also align you with the very heartbeat of Christ.
“The Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.” — Luke 19:10
If something in you is stirring right now… don’t ignore it.
Will you remain part of the few?
Or will you finally step in as a worker?
Say it plainly—“I won’t stay silent anymore.”
